newsitem.title: SPAIN: BBV firmer ahead of share split on July 19.
newsitem.headline: BBV firmer ahead of share split on July 19.

text.p: Shares in Spain's second-largest bank Banco Bilbao Vizcaya outperformed the market on Wednesday, as investors switched into the share before its split on July 19, analysts said.
"In BBV the split is coming up," said an analyst at a Spanish brokerage. "Everyone here likes splits and buys stock before the split."
Shares in BBV rose 400 pesetas, or 3.09 percent, to close at 13,340 pesetas, while the IBEX-35 index climbed just 72.01 points, or 1.02 percent, to 7,136.13 points.
"It's probably because of the split," another analyst said.
On July 19, the bank will reduce its nominal share value by 25 pesetas to 550 pesetas from 575. The 25 peseta difference will be paid back to shareholders.
Analysts downplayed talk among traders that BBV was benefitting from switching out of leading bank Santander, saying the latter's fall stemmed from profit-taking.
"It's weak on profit-taking. All the good news is discounted," he said.
Santander fell 45 pesetas, or 0.96 percent, to 4,650 pesetas.
Both groups are due to announce first-half results shortly, and analysts expect gains of 20.8 percent in Santander and of 25.7 percent in BBV.
"Results will be good in both cases," an analyst said.
